1	/**
     2	 * Static documentation strings for all Project Ledger MCP tools.
     3	 * Exported as TOOL_HELP and consumed by help.ts.
     4	 */
     5	import { PLAN_ARCHIVE_FILENAME, SYNTHESIS_ARCHIVE_FILENAME } from '../utils/constants.js';
     6	
     7	// Shared parameter descriptions reused across all tools that accept project resolution params.
     8	const CWD_PATH_PARAM =
     9	  '- **cwd_path** (string): Workspace root — auto-detects the active project. Pass this if you don\'t have project_path yet.';
    10	const PROJECT_PATH_PARAM =
    11	  '- **project_path** (string): Plan folder path — use if already known; takes precedence over cwd_path if both are provided.';
    12	
    13	export const TOOL_HELP: Record<string, string> = {
    14	  overview: `
    15	# Project Ledger MCP — Tool Reference
    16	
    17	## Path Parameters
    18	
    19	**Most tools accept \`project_path\` and/or \`cwd_path\`.** If you have \`project_path\` (the plan folder), use it — it's the fastest path. If you only know your workspace directory, pass \`cwd_path\` and the server auto-detects the active project. If you pass both, \`project_path\` takes precedence and \`cwd_path\` is ignored. The one exception is \`ledger_initialize_project\`, which requires \`project_path\` (the plan folder is being created and cannot be detected yet).
    20	
    21	## All Available Tools
    22	
    23	| Tool | Required Params | Purpose |
    24	|------|----------------|---------|
    25	| ledger_get_project_status | cwd_path or project_path | Read project overview |
    26	| ledger_initialize_project | project_path, plan_file | Create new project ledger |
    27	| ledger_list_projects | None (status filter optional) | List all tracked projects with status, dates, and plan paths |
    28	| ledger_complete_synthesis | cwd_path or project_path | Mark synthesis as generated; transitions project to COMPLETE |
    29	| ledger_get_work_package | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id | Read a work package's full detail |
    30	| ledger_list_work_packages | cwd_path or project_path | List work packages (optional: status, assigned_to filters) |
    31	| ledger_create_work_package | cwd_path or project_path, assigned_to, dependencies, acceptance_criteria, work_package_file | Create a new work package |
    32	| ledger_claim_work_package | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, agent | Claim a READY WP → IN_PROGRESS |
    33	| ledger_begin_work | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, agent_role | Claim + start pipeline in one atomic call |
    34	| ledger_update_work_package_status | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, status, agent | Update WP status |
    35	| ledger_start_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type | Start a pipeline for a work package (ordering determined by WP's active_pipeline_stages) |
    36	| ledger_complete_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, status, summary | Complete a pipeline |
    37	| ledger_cancel_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, reason | Cancel a stale IN_PROGRESS pipeline (sets to FAIL) |
    38	| ledger_update_pipeline_progress | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, summary | Update summary of IN_PROGRESS pipeline without completing it |
    39	| ledger_add_observation | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, pipeline_type, type, priority, note | Add observation to pipeline |
    40	| ledger_add_project_comment | cwd_path or project_path, type, priority, agent, note | Add project-level comment |
    41	| ledger_get_next_action | cwd_path or project_path, agent_role | Get next recommended action (optional: max_results for batch mode) |
    42	| ledger_get_handoff_status | cwd_path or project_path, current_agent | Check handoff status |
    43	| ledger_add_insight | scope, title, content, category, tags | Add a reusable insight to the knowledge base |
    44	| ledger_search_insights | query | Search the knowledge base (optional: scope, category, tags, repository_name, limit) |
    45	| ledger_list_insights | None required | List insights with optional filters and pagination |
    46	| ledger_update_insight | id | Update an existing insight by numeric ID |
    47	
    48	## Common Mistakes
    49	
    50	1. **Forgetting the "agent" parameter** — ledger_claim_work_package, ledger_update_work_package_status, and ledger_add_project_comment ALL require an "agent" param with your agent name.
    51	2. **Wrong pipeline type names** — Use exactly: "implementation", "qa", "security-audit", "code-review", "release-engineering", "documentation". Only the pipeline types listed in a WP's \`active_pipeline_stages\` are valid for that WP.
    52	3. **Trying to mark COMPLETE as the wrong terminal agent** — Only the agent owning the last active stage of the WP's pipeline can auto-finalize to COMPLETE. For the default 4-stage pipeline this is the Documentation agent. For non-standard compositions (e.g., verification-only \`["qa", "code-review"]\`), it is the agent owning the last active stage (e.g., Reviewer).
    53	4. **Starting a pipeline before claiming the WP** — WP must be IN_PROGRESS before starting a pipeline.
    54	5. **Not updating acceptance_criteria** — Use the acceptance_criteria_updates param in ledger_complete_pipeline to mark criteria as met before marking WP COMPLETE.
    55	6. **Starting pipelines out of order** — Pipelines must follow the WP's active stage order (a subsequence of: implementation → qa → security-audit → code-review → release-engineering → documentation). Starting a stage requires a PASS pipeline on the immediately preceding active stage. Starting a stage not in the WP's \`active_pipeline_stages\` is also rejected.
    56	7. **Setting WP to BLOCKED after a pipeline FAIL** — When QA or Reviewer fails a pipeline, do NOT set the WP to BLOCKED. Leave it as IN_PROGRESS so the Developer can find it via ledger_get_next_action and rework. BLOCKED should only be used for external blockers (missing APIs, pending decisions, etc.).
    57	8. **Test-only WP references non-existent production method** — When creating a WP whose \`active_pipeline_stages\` excludes "implementation" (test-only, verification-only, or documentation-only), verify that all methods/functions referenced in the WP's scope already exist in production code. If they don't, the WP needs the "implementation" stage — otherwise the Developer will silently expand scope by adding production code inside a non-implementation WP.
    58	
    59	## Workflow Order
    60	
    61	1. PM creates work packages (ledger_create_work_package), optionally specifying a custom \`active_pipeline_stages\` to compose the pipeline (defaults to \`["implementation","qa","code-review","documentation"]\`)
    62	2. Developer claims WP and starts pipeline in one call (\`ledger_begin_work\` type="implementation", agent_role="Developer"), completes pipeline (ledger_complete_pipeline). Note: starting a pipeline auto-updates assigned_to on the WP.
    63	3. QA starts pipeline (type="qa"), completes pipeline
    64	3a. *(Optional — only if WP's active_pipeline_stages includes "security-audit")* Security Auditor starts pipeline (type="security-audit"), completes pipeline
    65	4. Reviewer starts pipeline (type="code-review"), completes pipeline
    66	4a. *(Optional — only if WP's active_pipeline_stages includes "release-engineering")* Release Engineer starts pipeline (type="release-engineering"), completes pipeline
    67	5. Documentation starts pipeline (type="documentation"), completes pipeline — if status=PASS and all acceptance criteria are met, the WP is automatically transitioned to COMPLETE (auto-finalize, no separate ledger_update_work_package_status call needed)
    68	
    69	**Note:** The terminal agent (owner of the last active stage) triggers auto-finalize on PASS. For non-standard compositions (e.g., \`["qa","code-review"]\`), the Reviewer is the terminal agent who auto-finalizes the WP to COMPLETE.
    70	
    71	**Important:** Every ledger_complete_pipeline response includes a "--- NEXT STEP ---" guidance block telling you exactly what to do next. Follow it.
    72	
    73	## Rework After Pipeline FAIL
    74	
    75	When a QA or code-review pipeline completes with FAIL:
    76	- The agent who ran the failing pipeline should leave the WP as IN_PROGRESS (do NOT set to BLOCKED)
    77	- Call ledger_get_handoff_status to confirm handoff
    78	- The Developer will automatically see a REWORK action via ledger_get_next_action
    79	- The Developer re-implements, then the pipeline chain continues from QA again
    80	
    81	## Handoff Block Format
    82	
    83	Every agent must end their response with the handoff block returned by ledger_get_handoff_status. The block uses three fields:
    84	
    85	\`\`\`
    86	CURRENT AGENT: <current_agent>
    87	NEXT AGENT: <next_agent>
    88	STATUS: <status>
    89	\`\`\`
    90	
    91	- **current_agent**: The agent that just finished working (you)
    92	- **next_agent**: The agent that should pick up work next (derived from status)
    93	- **status**: The workflow status (e.g., READY_FOR_QA, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE)
    94	
    95	All three fields are returned by ledger_get_handoff_status — copy them verbatim.
    96	
    97	## Action Tool max_results
    98	
    99	- **ledger_get_next_action** (singular, default): Returns the first actionable WP for your role. Best for simple projects or when you process one WP at a time.
   100	- **ledger_get_next_action with max_results > 1**: Returns up to N actionable WPs as an array under the "actions" key. Best for projects with many independent WPs.

   102	## Storage Architecture
   103	
   104	All ledger files are stored **centrally** at \`{mcp-server}/storage/ledger/{slug}/\` — not inside the plan folder.
   105	- Plan folders remain purely human-readable markdown (no \`.ledger/\` subdirectory).
   106	- The storage root can be overridden at server startup with \`--ledger-dir <path>\`.
   107	
   108	### Files per project
   109	- **\`project-ledger.json\`** — root index (WP summaries, counters, status)
   110	- **\`WP-###.json\`** — individual work package detail files
   111	- **\`.meta.json\`** — per-project metadata created automatically on \`ledger_initialize_project\`; contains: \`slug\`, \`plan_path\`, \`status\`, \`date_created\`, \`last_updated\`, optional \`title\`. Used by \`ledger_list_projects\` for cross-project discovery.
   112	- **\`.lock\`** — file lock (managed automatically; do not edit)

   193	## Optional Parameters

   207	# ledger_create_work_package

   209	Create a new work package. WP ID is auto-generated.

   211	## Required Parameters

Each entry must be a valid pipeline type. The array must be a contiguous subsequence of the canonical ordering and cannot be empty, contain duplicates, or be out of order. A soft warning is emitted if "implementation" is included without "qa", or if only a single stage is specified.

   249	Claim a READY work package and start its pipeline in a single atomic call. Replaces the two-step \`ledger_claim_work_package\` + \`ledger_start_pipeline\` sequence.

251	If the WP is already IN_PROGRESS and assigned to you (idempotent re-entry), the claim phase is skipped and only the pipeline is started. The response includes a \`claimed: boolean\` field indicating whether the claim step ran.
   252	
   253	## Required Parameters
   254	${CWD_PATH_PARAM}
   255	${PROJECT_PATH_PARAM}
   256	- **work_package_id** (string): WP ID (format: WP-001)
   257	- **type** (string): Pipeline type — "implementation", "qa", "code-review", "documentation", "security-audit", or "release-engineering"
   258	- **agent_role** (string): Your agent role (e.g., "Developer", "QA") — used for both the claim and pipeline ownership guards
   259	
   260	## Guards Preserved
   261	- CLAIMABLE_ROLES — rejects roles not permitted to claim WPs
   262	- Assignment guard — WP must be assigned to your role (or already IN_PROGRESS and assigned to you)
   263	- Dependency completeness — all dependencies must be COMPLETE before claiming
   264	- Duplicate pipeline rejection — no two IN_PROGRESS pipelines of the same type
   265	- Pipeline ordering — determined per-WP by active_pipeline_stages (defaults to implementation → qa → code-review → documentation for standard WPs)
   266	- Rework circuit breaker — rejects if per-type rework count is at maximum
   267	- Agent role validation — pipeline type must match the expected owner role
   268	
   269	## Response
   270	Same shape as \`ledger_start_pipeline\` plus a \`claimed: boolean\` field.
   271	
   272	## Example: Claim and start implementation
   273	\`\`\`json
   274	{
   275	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   276	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   277	  "type": "implementation",
   278	  "agent_role": "Developer"
   279	}
   280	\`\`\`
   281	
   282	## Example: Start next pipeline (WP already IN_PROGRESS)
   283	\`\`\`json
   284	{
   285	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   286	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   287	  "type": "qa",
   288	  "agent_role": "QA"
   289	}
   290	\`\`\`
   291	`,
   292	
   293	  ledger_claim_work_package: `
   294	# ledger_claim_work_package
   295	
   296	Claim a READY work package → transitions to IN_PROGRESS.
   297	
   298	## Assignment Guard
   299	If the work package is already assigned to a different agent, the claim will be **rejected** unless you pass \`override: true\`. This prevents agents from silently re-assigning work packages outside their remit.
   300	
   301	## Required Parameters
   302	${CWD_PATH_PARAM}
   303	${PROJECT_PATH_PARAM}
   304	- **work_package_id** (string): WP ID (format: WP-001)
   305	- **agent** (string): ⚠️ REQUIRED — Your agent name (e.g., "Developer", "QA")
   306	
   307	## Optional Parameters
   308	- **override** (boolean): Set to \`true\` to claim a WP assigned to a different agent. Only the **Project Manager** and the **current assignee** may use \`override: true\`. Omit or set \`false\` otherwise.
   309	
   310	## Example
   311	\`\`\`json
   312	{
   313	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   314	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   315	  "agent": "Developer"
   316	}
   317	\`\`\`
   318	
   319	## Example: Override assignment
   320	\`\`\`json
   321	{
   322	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   323	  "work_package_id": "WP-007",
   324	  "agent": "Developer",
   325	  "override": true
   326	}
   327	\`\`\`
   328	`,
   329	
   330	  ledger_update_work_package_status: `
   331	# ledger_update_work_package_status
   332	
   333	Update a work package's status.
   334	
   335	## Required Parameters
   336	${CWD_PATH_PARAM}
   337	${PROJECT_PATH_PARAM}
   338	- **work_package_id** (string): WP ID (format: WP-001)
   339	- **status** (string): New status — "READY", "IN_PROGRESS", "COMPLETE", or "BLOCKED"
   340	- **agent** (string): ⚠️ REQUIRED — Your agent name (e.g., "Developer", "Documentation")
   341	
   342	## Optional Parameters
   343	- **blocked_by** (object): Required ONLY when setting status to "BLOCKED"
   344	
   345	## Rules
   346	- Only the Documentation agent can set status to "COMPLETE"
   347	- Only the Project Manager can set status to "CANCELLED"
   348	- Legal transitions: READY→IN_PROGRESS, READY→BLOCKED, READY→CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETE, IN_PROGRESS→BLOCKED, IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED, BLOCKED→IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED→READY, BLOCKED→CANCELLED, COMPLETE→IN_PROGRESS
   349	- CANCELLED is a terminal status — no outward transitions from CANCELLED are permitted
   350	- CANCELLED WPs satisfy dependency requirements (treated like COMPLETE for dependency checks)
   351	
   352	## Example: Mark COMPLETE (Documentation agent only)
   353	\`\`\`json
   354	{
   355	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   356	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   357	  "status": "COMPLETE",
   358	  "agent": "Documentation"
   359	}
   360	\`\`\`
   361	
   362	## Example: Mark BLOCKED
   363	\`\`\`json
   364	{
   365	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   366	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   367	  "status": "BLOCKED",
   368	  "agent": "Developer",
   369	  "blocked_by": {
   370	    "type": "technical",
   371	    "description": "Missing API endpoint"
   372	  }
   373	}
   374	\`\`\`
   375	`,
   376	
   377	  ledger_start_pipeline: `
   378	# ledger_start_pipeline
   379	
   380	Start a new pipeline for a work package. The WP must be IN_PROGRESS.
   381	
   382	## Required Parameters
   383	${CWD_PATH_PARAM}
   384	${PROJECT_PATH_PARAM}
   385	- **work_package_id** (string): WP ID (format: WP-001)
   386	- **type** (string): Pipeline type — "implementation", "qa", "code-review", "documentation", "security-audit", or "release-engineering"
   387	
   388	## Example
   389	\`\`\`json
   390	{
   391	  "project_path": "f:\\\\project\\\\docs\\\\agents\\\\plans\\\\2026-02-16-feature",
   392	  "work_package_id": "WP-001",
   393	  "type": "implementation"
   394	}
   395	\`\`\`
   396	
   397	## Prerequisites
   398	- WP must be IN_PROGRESS (use ledger_claim_work_package first if READY)
   399	- No duplicate in-progress pipeline of the same type allowed
   400	- **Pipeline ordering is enforced per-WP:** each stage must be preceded by a PASS on the immediately preceding active stage in the WP's active_pipeline_stages list. The default 4-stage order is implementation → qa → code-review → documentation, but WPs may define custom subsets or include security-audit and release-engineering.
